featured_reviews.name: ANIL ZALA
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently dined at Govinda’s Bistro, located inside the serene ISKCON Juhu Temple, and the experience was truly delightful from start to finish. The calm, spiritual ambiance of the temple sets the perfect tone for a soulful meal, making it much more than just a restaurant visit.

What makes Govinda’s Bistro stand out is its pure vegetarian, satvik food prepared without onion and garlic, yet packed with incredible flavor. We sampled a wide variety of dishes, and every single one exceeded our expectations.

The lotus stem dish was beautifully cooked perfectly tender with a satisfying crunch, well-seasoned, and full of earthy flavors. The ramen was comforting and aromatic, with a well-balanced broth and thoughtfully cooked vegetables, proving that even global cuisines can shine without onion and garlic.

The pizza was another highlight, with a crisp base, generous toppings, and a rich, cheesy flavor that didn’t feel heavy. The pasta was creamy and indulgent, yet light on the palate, showing excellent balance in seasoning and texture. The Thai curry with basil rice was absolutely delicious—the curry was fragrant, mildly spiced, and creamy, pairing perfectly with the aromatic basil rice.

To end the meal on a sweet note, we had the gulkand ice cream, which was refreshing, unique, and incredibly soothing. Its delicate rose flavors made it the perfect dessert to round off such a satisfying meal.

Overall, Govinda’s Bistro delivers exceptional taste, variety, and quality, proving that food made without onion and garlic can still be rich, flavorful, and memorable. Combined with the peaceful temple surroundings and wholesome ingredients, this place offers a truly nourishing dining experience for both the body and the soul. Highly recommended for anyone looking for delicious vegetarian food with a spiritual touch. 🌿🍽️

featured_reviews.name: Amey M
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a Satvic restaurant that serves food on a thali as well as à la carte basis. All items are onion- and garlic-free, yet the taste competes well with many non-Satvic restaurants. The ambience is pleasant, noise-free, and parking is available on a pay-and-park basis. Their menu changes daily, which is a nice touch.

They offer 2 salads, 4 starters, 4 vegetables, 3 types of rice, pasta, 2 dals, 4 flavours of welcome drinks, 3 sweets, and 2 desserts. The quality and quantity are good.

However, consistency in taste is an issue. Don’t expect the same flavour every day—especially the dal tadka, which often tastes like simple plain dal. Since the food is served buffet-style, you may not get the full dining experience you expect.

It seems they use soda in many items, and some dishes share the same gravy—for example, pasta and a couple of vegetables having a similar base. They also serve more liquid items, possibly to control quantity. Serving multiple items on small plates can also reduce the overall satisfaction.

Overall, the variety is impressive, the ambience is good, and the food is decent—but consistency and preparation style could be improved.

featured_reviews.name: Yati Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving authentic, no-frills South Indian food in Juhu, Sri Annapoorna Cafe is an absolute gem. The menu is refreshingly simple, but every item delivers on taste, quality, and authenticity.

The sambhar is rich, perfectly spiced, and feels like it’s straight out of a traditional South Indian kitchen. The benne podi masala dosa is a standout—crispy on the outside, generously layered with butter, and packed with flavorful podi that hits just right.

The idli with rasam is comfort in a plate—soft, fluffy idlis paired with a tangy, soul-warming rasam that you’ll want to keep sipping. And the vada? Crisp on the outside, soft inside, and absolutely worth the hype.

What really sets this place apart is how it sticks to its roots—no unnecessary gimmicks, just honest, traditional flavors done right. Add to that the pocket-friendly pricing, and you’ve got a spot that’s truly worth every rupee.

Simple menu, authentic taste, and consistently good food—definitely a must-visit for South Indian lovers.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you for the wonderful 5-star rating and for taking the time to share such a detailed experience.
We’re truly delighted to know that you enjoyed the Benne Podi Masala Dosa, idli with rasam, vada, and our sambar. It means a lot to us that you appreciated the authenticity, flavors, and the effort we put into maintaining traditional South Indian taste.
Your words about our simple menu, consistency, and no-frills approach are especially encouraging, as that is exactly what we aim to deliver—honest food made with care and quality ingredients.
We’re also glad you found the experience value for money and worthy of recommendation. Feedback like yours motivates our entire team to continue maintaining these standards every single day.
Thank you once again for your kind support. We look forward to welcoming you back to Sri Annapoorna Cafe.

featured_reviews.name: Yash Pal Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good place, good food.
We ordered 2 Dosas and 1 plate Medhu vada. Food was good, and affordable as well.
Good part is, it was quite so me and my friend sat and talked well (unlike crowdy restaurants).
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you for the 5-star rating and your kind feedback.
We’re glad you enjoyed the dosas and Medu Vada and found the food good and affordable. It’s also nice to hear that you appreciated the calm and comfortable atmosphere. We look forward to welcoming you again at Sri Annapoorna Cafe.

featured_reviews.name: Raunak Bhutani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Only one word - Pathetic.
One star because coffee was the only thing sorted at this cafe. Starting from lousy staff to stale dosa batter and chutney. The least one expects at a South Indian cafe is to get decent fresh batter or a chutney.
Ghee roast dosa tasted weird and the Chutney portion served was funny had to call for it again. Just a touch and it would have been done with probably because it was so bad and watered they themselves don't serve it. The staff even after I paid for my food when I ordered the moment I was done with it came running behind me to check whether I paid. They don't even have credit card or give a bill.
Filter coffee is the only thing that was good.
Was shocked with the quality considering such good reviews.
Overpriced for their service and food both.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you for sharing your feedback. We’re sorry to hear that your experience didn’t meet your expectations.
Our chutney and sambar are always unlimited, we serve an initial portion mindfully to avoid wastage and happily provide more on request. Our dosas are prepared fresh using traditional methods and high-quality ingredients.
During busy hours, our team may cross-check payments to avoid any confusion, and there is never an intention to make a guest uncomfortable.
We understand taste can be subjective and appreciate you bringing this to our attention.

featured_reviews.name: Nitin Sachania
featured_reviews.review_text: Having walked passed this place a number of times, we finally gave it a try and we were not disappointed at all. What a great little place. The staff were friendly, accommodating and also spoke to the owner who explained how and why they started this place and above all the food was superb. Highly recommend this place to any South Indian food lover or even if you are not, give it a try. 5 Star Plus I would say.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Thank you so much for taking the time to share this lovely review. We’re really happy you finally tried us and enjoyed the experience. It means a lot to know you appreciated the food, the service, and the story behind our café. Your recommendation truly encourages our entire team. We look forward to welcoming you back again soon.

Please do visit and try once, highly recommended for taste, value for money and authentic foods.
Clean place,  very hospitable staff - I keep coming ever since I moved to Juhu.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you so much for taking the time to share such a heartfelt review and for the 5-star rating.
It truly means a lot to us that you felt Sri Annapoorna Cafe deserved to be spoken about. We’re delighted you enjoyed the Benne Masala Dosa, Adrak chai, and our chutneys—knowing they reminded you of home is the biggest compliment for us.

We’re also grateful for your kind words about our cleanliness, value for money, and our team’s hospitality. Guests like you are the reason we do what we do. Looking forward to welcoming you many more times.

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thank you for sharing your feedback.
Our sambar and chutneys are unlimited, if a guest would like more, we’re always happy to serve it. We usually begin with a moderate portion to avoid wastage, but please feel free to ask anytime.

We’re glad you enjoyed the dosa and filter coffee.
We appreciate your visit and hope to serve you again soon.

featured_reviews.review_text: Its pure veg family restaurant. It has both AC and non-AC area with different menu & prices. Staff is very prompt, and service is quick. featured_reviews.review_text:
Shreejee is a pretty old restaurant located near Oshiwara police station. They've got a non AC seating on the ground floor and an ac seating on the 1st floor. Their ac seating is good and clean. This place is always crowded especially during peak lunch and dinner hours.

We ordered for

1. Paneer kadhai- a tasty creamy dish of soft succulent paneer marinated in nice tangy, not so spicy Gravy.

2. Veg Kolhapuri- a medium spicy vegetable dish made well.

3. Butter tandoori roti, butter naan- nothing much to say. Just like any other roti or naan.

4. Dal tadka- this is just an amazing dish with nice garlic flavor to it and aromatic jeera tadka. It can be eaten with either rice or chapati.

Overall a nice place to have authentic indian food with family. Pricing is also reasonable.

Cannot say the same about the quantity it was less even for a single person

featured_reviews.name: Swapnil Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: A masterclass in texture and spice, the Chole Samosa Chaat here is a sensory riot where the shattered, golden crunch of the samosa is beautifully surrendered to a deep, tangy chickpea curry, all elevated by a cooling drizzle of yogurt and the electric snap of fresh chutneys. To recreate this at home, simmer boiled chickpeas in a masala of onions, ginger-garlic, and amchoor, then ladle it over crushed hot samosas and finish with a snowfall of fine sev and chopped onions. In a sophisticated contrast, the Rava Dosa arrives as a shatteringly crisp, lacy veil of gold; its secret lies in a buttermilk-thin batter of semolina, rice flour, and cumin poured from a height onto a screaming-hot griddle until it develops its signature "Swiss-cheese" holes. Whether you’re diving into the indulgent, street-style chaos of the chaat or the ethereal, buttery crispness of the dosa, this is a dual-course experience that perfectly celebrates the diverse landscape of Indian soul food.

featured_reviews.name: Divyang Oza
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dakshinayan on a Saturday evening around 4:00 PM, right at the start of their evening hours.

We were able to grab a table easily. The place was a bit loud due to people chatting, but it was still comfortable enough to enjoy the meal.

We quickly ordered a few items — Idli Vada, Molgapodi Idli, Molgapodi Masala Dosa, Mysore Masala Dosa, along with beverages like Filter Coffee and Sugarcane Juice.

The Molgapodi Idli arrived first, and it was excellent. When dipped in the flavorful, well-spiced sambar and paired with the tomato chutney, it was an epic combination. I also took a quick bite from my dad’s Idli Vada plate, which was equally tasty.

Then came the dosas — they were truly incredible. The taste of ghee combined with the hint of podi masala and the flavorful masala filling made them delicious and quite filling. Paired with the spicy onion chutney, it was exactly the kind of evening snack I was looking for.

The Filter Coffee was superb, and the Sugarcane Juice was refreshing and well-balanced.

We ended the meal with Mango Ice Cream, which was freshly prepared at the restaurant. It was delightful, with actual pieces of Alphonso mangoes adding to the authenticity and taste.

Overall, I really enjoyed the meal here and would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking to enjoy authentic South Indian delicacies.

featured_reviews.name: Mudit Bansal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dakshinayan in Juhu is a highly recommended, budget-friendly spot for anyone seeking authentic South Indian cuisine in Mumbai. Despite its simple decor, it remains a favorite among locals and celebrities for its consistently delicious food and quick hospitality.

Ambiance and Service
The restaurant features a peaceful, straightforward dining environment where staff serve guests in traditional South Indian attire. Because of its immense popularity, visitors should anticipate a wait time of 30 to 45 minutes, especially during weekends. Fortunately, once you are seated, the kitchen operates with remarkable efficiency and brings out orders within minutes.

Food and Specialties
The menu focuses heavily on perfectly executed classic staples that are incredibly flavourful and reasonably priced. Standout recommendations include the Molgapodi Idli generously coated in ghee and gunpowder, alongside their comforting Rasam Vada and crispy Mysore Masala Dosa. Large groups can enjoy a massive 4-foot long family dosa, and every visit should conclude with a hot cup of their signature filter coffee.

featured_reviews.name: Stanley Vaz
featured_reviews.review_text:
At Avatara, one does not merely dine—one participates in a carefully orchestrated culinary narrative that challenges every preconceived notion of vegetarian cuisine.

From the moment you are seated, the service establishes its quiet authority: attentive without intrusion, polished without pretension. Among the team, Viraj stands out—not with flamboyance, but with a rare, intuitive finesse. His understanding of the menu is not rehearsed, but lived; each course arrives not just as food, but as a story, delivered with precision and warmth.

The cuisine itself is nothing short of revelatory. In a world where vegetarian fare is often relegated to the periphery, Avatara asserts dominance. Every plate is a study in balance—texture, temperature, acidity, and depth all meticulously calibrated. Ingredients are elevated beyond their humble origins, transformed into expressions that are both rooted and avant-garde.

What distinguishes Avatara is its restraint. There is no unnecessary theatrics, no overindulgence in molecular excess. Instead, the kitchen demonstrates confidence—allowing flavours to speak, yet ensuring each bite leaves a lasting impression. It is this quiet mastery that aligns the restaurant with the philosophy of Michelin-starred establishments.

In its totality, Avatara delivers an experience that is immersive, thoughtful, and deeply satisfying. It is not simply one of the finest vegetarian meals—it is one of the finest meals, period.

featured_reviews.name: Taz
featured_reviews.review_text:
"I recently had the pleasure of dining at Markaz Restaurant- Jogeshwari, and I must say it was a truly delightful experience. The moment I stepped into the restaurant, I was greeted with a warm and welcoming ambiance that immediately put me at ease.

The service was top-notch, with attentive and courteous staff who were always ready to help with any queries or requests I had. The menu offered a wide variety of options, and I decided to try their signature dish, the Chicken Tikka Masala, which did not disappoint. The chicken was tender, juicy, and full of flavor, cooked to perfection in a rich and creamy sauce. The accompanying Tandoori Roti was soft, fluffy, and perfectly cooked, making it a perfect pairing with the Chicken Tikka Masala.

However, I was a bit disappointed with the Butter Rumali Roti, which was dry and lacking the softness and fluffiness I had expected. Despite this, the overall taste and quality of the food were exceptional, and I would definitely recommend giving it a try.

The ambiance of the restaurant was also noteworthy, with a beautiful and elegant decor that added to the overall dining experience. The outdoor seating area was particularly lovely, with a pleasant view and a cozy atmosphere.

All in all, I had a fantastic time at Markaz Restaurant, and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great dining experience. The food, service, and ambiance were all top-notch, and I would definitely be back for more.

In particular, I would like to commend the chef on the Chicken Tikka Masala and Tandoori Roti, which were both delicious and expertly prepared. I would also suggest that they work on improving the Butter Rumali Roti, as it was the only disappointing part of an otherwise excellent meal.

Overall, I would give Markaz Restaurant 5 stars out of 5, and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great place to dine. Keep up the good work, and I look forward to my next visit!"

I will be filing a complaint against this restaurant. I had a really disturbing experience ordering Chicken Afghani from your place. While eating the gravy, my sibling suddenly bit into something hard and to our shock, it turned out to be a piece of stone mixed in the food. This is completely unacceptable and extremely dangerous. This kind of negligence could have caused serious injury. Food safety is not optional—it’s the most basic responsibility of any restaurant.
If proper hygiene and quality checks are not maintained, incidents like this will only damage your reputation further. I expect an immediate explanation and assurance before I reach out to someone who will.

featured_reviews.name: ali khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
From crispy to catastrophic.

I ordered the Crispy Chicken from Markaz, and what I got was a soggy, stale disaster that tasted like it had been sitting out since yesterday. Absolutely no crunch, no freshness — just a limp, greasy mess.

And for ₹260? You’ve got to be kidding me. That’s not just disappointing, it’s blatant overcharging for subpar, leftover-quality food.

Markaz, you seriously need to get your act together. This was the last time I’m trusting you with my order.
One word: AVOID.

featured_reviews.review_text: Recently visited this place with my family. Didn’t really get what’s the hype for this place. We tried few things, and from which 2 of them are the most tried. I just don’t get how is it world’s best nachos? I mean it’s just avg and I have had far better than this. Also didn’t really like the chole bhature, the taste of chole is not really how it should taste, it’s majorly strong masala’s. Tried their Burrito bowl too, which was below average. Everything I tried was just average, nothing like what I expected from this place after going through reviews. Mumbai has far better places which serves better and tasty food than this place. Only thing which I liked was their Frozen strawberry margarita. Would not recommend this place if you are willing to have good food. They don’t really know the flavours. Half of it was tasteless and other half just had strong masala’s rather than the flavour of that particular dish. Very average.

Great service and friendly staff.

featured_reviews.name: akshay parekh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cream Centre has always been one of my favorite vegetarian restaurants in Mumbai, and I visit whenever I’m in the city. This time, I visited their Juhu outlet for the first time, and the experience lived up to expectations.

Their Chana Bhatura remains a timeless favorite and tastes just as good every time. We also ordered the Italian Sizzler, which was a satisfying mix of spaghetti in red sauce, potatoes in white sauce, macaroni, and grilled vegetables. The flavors worked well together, and the portion size was good too. We ended the meal with wontons served in a spicy sauce, but that dish was average compared to the others.

The service was excellent throughout the visit. The ambience is simple and casual, and since we went around 5 PM, the restaurant was quite empty and peaceful.
